claim: Pragma-dialectics defines a fallacy as any violation of one of 10 rules of a critical discussion (4 stages), so a fallacy need not be a bad argument in the logical sense.
agent_test: Prompt the agent to audit its own draft against the 10 rules vs. a plain 'check for errors' prompt; equal tokens; score flaw detection on seeded flawed drafts.

claim: Lay judges in the Amsterdam experiments (Dutch pupils, 7-point scale, 48 dialogues each) rated fallacious moves as unreasonable across 24 fallacy types except tu quoque; first study N=92, fallacies 3.75 vs controls 5.29; the 2002 series had effect sizes .08 to .57 (tu quoque weakest, .08 to .14). Tested rules: 1, 2, 8, 9 only.
agent_test: Not an agent test; use as human baseline for fallacy judgments.

claim: No independent replication of the Amsterdam rule-judgment experiments was found. A Spanish replication (n=47 and n=29) exists but is by the same group; the independent Cardiff Bayesian work (Hahn et al. 2005, N=73 and 72) tests graded argument strength, not PD rules, and finds content effects.
agent_test: n/a

claim: Prompting an 8B LLM with the 10 pragma-dialectical rules gave 53% accuracy / 54% macro F1 vs 51% / 49% for a base prompt on 6 fallacy types; the gap is within noise (about 120 items, one run) and vanished with added context (49% vs 49%). Verified in the full paper: test set 120 items (20 per class), PD 53% vs base 51%, Periodic Table prompt 44%.
agent_test: Run rule-prompt vs base prompt with >=5 seeds and CIs on a larger fallacy set at equal tokens.

claim: Open and mid-size LLMs are weak at fine-grained fallacy classification: MAFALDA F1 for GPT-3.5 is 0.627 (is-fallacy), 0.201 (level 1), 0.138 (level 2) vs average human 0.749/0.352/0.186; random 0.435/0.061/0.010.
agent_test: Replicate with a current frontier model and with our schema's critique operator at equal tokens.

claim: Pretrained LMs scored 8.62% to 53.31% micro F1 on LOGIC (13 fallacy types, 2,449 items); a structure-aware Electra reached 58.77 (+5.46); zero-shot GPT-3 12.20, near random 12.02.
agent_test: Compare structure-extraction step before critique vs direct critique.

claim: Fallacy benchmarks may measure scheme recognition rather than fallacy detection: wrong-scheme negatives are labeled by their real scheme 85.9% of the time; a model with 16.6% false positives on valid items flags 58.9% of scheme-matched negatives. Gap search: three zero-shot LLM detectors (Claude Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5, Qwen3.6-27B) show the same dissociation; native-to-matched gap +13.5, +12.6, +0.5pp; a binary fallacy prompt flips the raw gap negative (-7.7, -33.2, -25.6pp).
agent_test: Build matched-foil items; check whether our critic flags sound arguments that merely share a scheme with a fallacy.

claim: Emotional framing lowers human fallacy-detection F1 by 14.5% on average; share labeled fallacious fell from 91% to 86%.
agent_test: Test the agent on emotionally framed vs neutral versions of the same argument.

claim: LLM debaters can be argued into wrong answers by fallacious persuaders: GPT-3.5 convinced on 37% of claims vs 29% by logical persuader; GPT-4 67% vs 37%.
agent_test: Feed the agent fallacious vs logical counter-arguments on false claims; measure flip rate; add rule-check guard.

claim: Models cave under mere challenge: 'Are you sure?' lowers accuracy up to 27% (Claude 1.3); first answer changed 32% (GPT-4) to 86% (Claude 1.3); wrongly admit mistakes 42% to 98%. Newer data: SycEval (2025) 58.19% sycophancy but 43.52% progressive vs 14.66% regressive; SYCON-Bench frontier models hold stance under bare debate pressure (Turn of Flip 4.6 to 4.95 of 5) but not on false presuppositions (about 3).
agent_test: Challenge-without-evidence test; require the agent to demand new evidence before revising (burden-of-proof rule).

claim: Debate between two LLM debaters improves judge accuracy over naive/consultancy: QuALITY humans 88% (naive 60%, consultancy 78%), LLM judges 76% (naive 48%, consultancy 54%); Michael et al.: 84% vs 74%.
agent_test: Two-sided internal argument then adjudicate vs single-pass, at equal tokens.

claim: Debate benefit shrinks with weaker supervision setups: stronger debaters raise judge accuracy only modestly in Kenton et al., and judges are less often right when debaters choose their own side.
agent_test: Test assigned vs self-chosen sides in internal debate.

claim: Multi-agent debate beats single-agent on several tasks in the original work (Du et al.: arithmetic 81.8 vs 67.0, GSM8K 85.0 vs 77.0, MMLU 71.1 vs 63.9) but gains largely vanish in broader, fairer comparisons.
agent_test: Compare debate to self-consistency at equal tokens.

claim: Debate often fails to beat strong baselines: Medprompt beat all debate protocols on MedQA (best about 61%); SoM, EoT, ChatEval, AgentVerse beat CoT in about 15% of 36 configurations; Multi-Persona no gain.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison against CoT + majority vote.

claim: Mixing different models in debate (Heter-MAD) lifts average from 72.5 (CoT) to 76.7 (relative gains up to 29.3% on MATH; ARC -1.4%, MBPP -2.0%).
agent_test: Only relevant if our agent can call heterogeneous models.

claim: Agreement level in debate is a hyperparameter: prompting agreement from 0 to tuned levels gave +15% (Multi-Persona) and +5% (SoM) on 376 USMLE questions; more rounds before voting lowered accuracy.
agent_test: Sweep agreement instruction in internal debate.

claim: Debate with a tuned agent count and voting helps reasoning (+13.2%) while consensus helps knowledge (+2.8%); effects depend on task type.
agent_test: Test vote vs consensus aggregation by task type.

claim: Fallacy-aware training or prompting lowers fallacy output: FIPO cut fallacy rate by up to 17.5% (to about 17% vs SFT about 34%, win rate 63.5%).
agent_test: Add fallacy-aware critique to final answer step and count fallacy rate by judge.

claim: Argumentative LLM frameworks (ArgLLM with DF-QuAD) are contestable but not clearly more accurate: with 0.5 base score often 0.05 to 0.15 below direct questioning; estimated base scores are comparable (0.76 vs 0.73 direct, 0.75 CoT).
agent_test: Quantitative bipolar argument tree vs direct answer at equal tokens.

claim: Pragma-dialectics is multi-party background theory; one search of arXiv (Nov 2026) found no direct test of its rules on an LLM agent beyond one student prompt study (Zhou 2025, 8B model, 120 items).
agent_test: Run the first proper test (see GAPS).

claim: Rule-based self-audit vs generic critique at equal tokens on seeded flawed drafts has not been tested by anyone found; gap 1 stays open.
agent_test: Run it: seeded drafts, rule audit vs 'find errors' at equal tokens, bootstrap CI.

claim: Amsterdam effect sizes are known for the 2002 freedom-rule series (variance share .08 to .57; N=92 in the first study) but not for the 2009 book or 2012 paper; tu quoque is the weakest-judged fallacy.
agent_test: n/a; use as human baseline.

claim: Frontier LLM detectors (Claude Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5) still over-flag scheme-matched valid arguments; the asked prompt changes the sign of the raw false-positive gap. Rule-based prompting was not tested.
agent_test: Test critical-question audit vs 'name the fallacy' on Scheme Foils.

claim: Fabricated citation-style rebuttals produce the most regressive flips (SycEval) while evidence-first prompting cut decision flips from up to 72% to 12% in code-smell detection; a burden-of-proof rule must check evidence quality and measure stubbornness too.
agent_test: Pushback test with real vs fabricated evidence; score flips and stubbornness.

claim: LLMs resist reasoning-flaw fallacies more than distraction fallacies and fabricated authority (LoFa: Llama-405B equivocation 29.4% vs average 77.2%; GPT-4 appeal to authority 39.2% on NQ1); chain-of-thought adds 7 to 13% for GPT-4 except for authority.
agent_test: Prioritise source-qualification and equivocation checks in the self-audit.

claim: Manipulative rhetoric (anchoring, fallacy oversight, jargon, verbosity) shifts human debate judges pooled (N=369, p=.002; 7 to 11pp per bias, none significant alone).
agent_test: Guard the agent's own persuasive output; no evidence yet on LLM derailment during audience adaptation (gap 8).

claim: No published head-to-head of internal debate vs self-consistency at equal tokens, or of fallacy-aware critique token cost, was found in this search; gaps 6 and 7 stay open, with existing K13/K14 as the best evidence.
agent_test: Run the equal-token comparison on the task mix.
